import pytest

if getattr(pytest, "use_correct", False):
    from correct_python_programs.find_in_sorted import find_in_sorted
else:
    from python_programs.find_in_sorted import find_in_sorted


def test_attack_1():
    # empty array must return -1, not raise
    assert find_in_sorted([], 1) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([], 0) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([], -5) == -1


def test_attack_2():
    # single-element arrays: found and not-found
    assert find_in_sorted([42], 42) == 0
    assert find_in_sorted([1], 2) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([5], 3) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([5], 5) == 0


def test_attack_3():
    # x greater than all elements -> original bug recursed on binsearch(mid, end)
    assert find_in_sorted([1, 2, 3], 10) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([2, 4, 6, 8], 10) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([2, 4, 6, 8], 9) == -1
    # x smaller than all elements
    assert find_in_sorted([5, 6, 7], 1) == -1


def test_attack_4():
    # x in a gap that forces a right-step on a size-1 interval
    assert find_in_sorted([1, 3], 2) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([1, 2], 3) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([1, 3], 4) == -1
    assert find_in_sorted([1, 3], 0) == -1


def test_attack_5():
    # first / last / middle present - catches off-by-one exclusive-end errors
    arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    assert find_in_sorted(arr, 1) == 0
